source.title: Reformulation for Pretraining Data Augmentation
source.authors: Xintong Hao; Ruijie Zhu; Ge Zhang; Ke Shen; Cheng-Gang Li

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own mismatch between held-out validation loss and downstream benchmark performance, qualifying the claim that downstream performance is predictable from pretraining loss. It does not fit or test scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-loss curves across training conditions and explicitly notes higher validation losses alongside improved benchmark performance. It does not fit power laws, test extrapolation, or evaluate compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Loss values are not numerically reported in the text.
record.test_reason: This is a data-augmentation paper (MGA reformulation). It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as motivation. It fits no power law, extrapolation or allocation, and makes no claim of predictable downstream scaling. The one relevant finding is that MGA models have higher validation loss but better benchmark scores. That loss is measured on held-out fineweb-edu, a domain whose training share MGA cuts from 80.89% to 16.29% (Table 5). So the gap reflects a shift in the training data mixture, compared across recipes rather than across scale. It is not a test of whether downstream performance tracks pretraining loss or scale (V6), so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The main conclusion is that MGA reformulation beats naive repetition and upsampling in data-constrained training up to 13B, with gains that grow with model size. On validation loss, the authors argue that the higher loss on real-data validation sets reflects a different learning strategy rather than model collapse, and that validation loss alone may not fully reflect performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates data augmentation through genre-audience reformulation and training comparisons; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation-loss patterns differ across validation datasets; the paper reports a scale-dependent reversal on python-edu between smaller models and the 1.7B model.

fits_no_version.finding: MGA-Expansion models score higher on benchmarks but show higher validation loss on fineweb-edu and open-web-math than baseline. On python-edu, MGA loss is worse at 134M/377M and better at 1.7B (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across different pretraining data mixtures, held-out loss on a fixed domain does not rank models by downstream benchmark performance.

record.problems: The validation-loss results are presented mainly in figures and lack numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study does not perform scaling-law fits or test loss predictions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version rows were extracted: the paper's other benchmark comparisons and loss curves do not test power-law scaling, extrapolation, architecture sensitivity, or compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
Architecture shape is not varied at fixed size.
Repeated and synthetic data regimes are studied via benchmark curves, but no power-law form is fitted.
Benchmarks rise with model size (377M–13B, Fig. 3/12/13), but no predictive fit is made. Loss–benchmark predictability at matched training distributions is not tested.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 'tests'/T5 classification over-reads a cross-data-mixture loss/benchmark mismatch as a test of loss-based downstream predictability. The paper's own 'N-scaling'/'D-scaling' language refers to benchmark gains of its method, not scaling-law fits.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or test of held-out loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No predictions from small-run fits are compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fit of optimal parameter and token counts.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns text pretraining with reformulated and repeated data but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in these regimes.
The study notes a validation-loss/benchmark mismatch for its data conditions, but does not fit a predictive relationship or test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across fitting choices or setups.

rows.note: The text states the mismatch but gives no numerical validation-loss values. This qualifies loss-based downstream predictability in this data setting; predictability from scale is not tested.
rows.check: Compares data recipes, not scale or matched pretraining loss. The validation set is fineweb-edu, whose share of training was deliberately cut in the MGA arm, so higher loss there is an expected distribution-shift effect. No loss values are given; the curves appear only in Figure 5. The size_stated field is fine (134M/377M/1.7B). The 'partial' state cannot be assessed against V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
